_niush_ink_.historical_summary:
Die Posts drehen sich hauptsächlich um kleine, illustrative und blackwork Tattoos in Hamburg, darunter Wannado-Designs, Custom-Tattoos, Giveaways, Buchungsaufrufe sowie Tier-, Anime- und Popkultur-Motive wie Katzen, Gänse, Pilze, Moomin, Zelda, Pokémon, Apothecary Diaries und Frieren. Der Schreibstil ist locker, freundlich und emojisprühend, oft mit Hashtags, direkter Ansprache und spielerischen Ausrufen; emotional überwiegen Dankbarkeit, Begeisterung und Nähe zu Kund:innen. Interaktionspräferenzen zeigen sich in Einladungen zu DM-Fragen, Anpassungen von Wannados, Interesse an Custom-Anfragen, Gewinnspielbeteiligung und klarem Hinweis, dass Anfragen über das Buchungsformular laufen, während Story-Highlights Termine und Designs zeigen.
Accounts this user follows often involve tattoo-related content, especially abstract tattoo designs.

asapconnections.description: ASAP’s mission is to help local farms thrive, link farmers to markets and supporters, and build healthy communities through connections to local food.

DVebukzkknC.content:
You can find details about a farm’s CSA season dates and payment structure in its CSA description in the online Local Food Guide. Start at asapconnections.org/csa, select your region, and click the name of the farm to view the full listing.

The CSA season typically begins in April or May, around the same time that seasonal farmers markets reopen, and lasts for 20-26 weeks. Some farms offer a fall extension, often as an add-on to the regular season. There are even a few farms that have winter or year-round produce CSAs! Look at the fall/winter column in ASAP’s CSA charts.

Now is the time to sign up for a regular season CSA share! If your first choice farm has already sold out, look for a newer farm that is still building a customer base.

Paying before the season starts is fundamental to the CSA model, but some farms do offer installment or pay-as-you-go plans. A few farms have a work-trade option to assist with on-farm tasks in exchange for a reduced price or free share.

Some farms set aside shares to donate to feeding sites or community members in need, and you may choose to pay toward those. Ask if the farm has the means to donate missed shares, such as when you’re on vacation.

DVjnpNSkj6-.content:
If you’ve been online lately, you may have seen 2026 declared as the year of the cabbage, but foodies and farmers market goers know that cabbage never really needed to be trending. Long before social media anointed the humble, layered globe as the vegetable of the moment, communities across the world relied on cabbage as a winter staple and a nourishing crop that has carried families through the coldest months of the year.

Cabbage belongs to the Brassica family—the same plant lineage that includes broccoli, kale, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, and many Asian greens. So whether you're making Polish-inspired cabbage and kielbasa, Korean kimchi, or a simple stir-fry with bok choy, you're cooking with a long history of brassicas. 

Read more about cabbage a bok choy, including recipes, in this week's roundup of What's Fresh at asaponnections.org.

Not in Buncombe? Search for markets across the region at appalachiangrown.org.

Note that @blackmountainmarket reopens for the season tomorrow, March 7, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Find the market at @foothillsgrange and Downtown Black Mountain.

DWHgWEHFJMt.content:
March is a month of transitions. The days stretch longer, the soil begins to warm, and the first signs of spring arrive at farmers markets and on our tables. 

When the busyness of spring starts to take over, sometimes dinner looks like what the internet may call “fridge foraging” or “girl dinner.” These meals bring together low-effort options assembled from random items in the fridge or pantry instead of a traditional structured meal. It can be a fun and non-restrictive way to eat what you love, what’s available to you, and without the stress of cooking something so elaborate. It’s also a creative way to reduce your home’s food waste. 

Sometimes, busy families just need to throw together an easy smorgasbord with lots of options! Check out these market goods ideas in this week's roundup of What's Fresh at asapconnections.org.

Not in Buncombe? Search for markets across the region at appalachiangrown.org.

DWUUm4YDhU4.content:
It’s Spring! 🌱 That means it’s time to get those seeds started. This DIY newspaper plant pot is a fun idea to do with the kids in your life. Plus, it’s cheap and easy to make! All you need is newspaper, a cup, seeds, soil, and water. 

🌱Step 1: Rip your newspaper in half and use a few sheets for each pot. 
🌱Step 2: Roll your cup on the newspaper but leave a little space at the top. 
🌱Step 3: Fold the newspaper into the open part of the cup. 
🌱Step 4: Remove the cup, reach your hand inside, and push the newspaper down to create a bottom. 
🌱Step 5: Fill your pot with potting soil.
🌱Step 6: Pick out some spring seeds and plant a few in the pot.
🌱Step 7: Water your seeds and place them in a sunny place in your house to watch them sprout and grow! Water regularly. Once the threat of frost has passed, you can plant them directly into the soil and they will biodegrade. 

Find seed starting guides and more activity ideas at growing-minds.org.

#seedstarting #gardeningforkids #diy

DXKcx-ojL75.content:
Meet and welcome one of the new members of ASAP's Board of Directors! 

Amy Yaroch is the Chief Executive Officer of Center for Nutrition & Health Impact and we are excited for her to bring her expertise and insight to our mission. We asked her a little about herself and this is what she had to say!

Q: What are you up to when you’re not at our board meetings? 
A:  Hiking and getting outdoors to enjoy all that Western North Carolina has to offer, including visiting our amazing farmers markets. I am so happy that the East Asheville Tailgate Market started back up. I try to swing by every Friday afternoon (when I am not traveling) to pick up local goodies.

Q: Why is ASAP important to you?
A:  Much of my research and evaluation over the last several years has focused on increasing fruit and vegetable intake, especially among populations who don’t have that access. ASAP is all about fulfilling that mission in Western North Carolina. I am so excited to be on the Board of Directors for ASAP since it aligns so well with my work and personal interests including supporting farmers, consumers, and others in my community.

Q: What’s your favorite local food dish? 
A:  During summer’s peak, I am always so excited to visit the farmers market to get local peaches and heirloom tomatoes. If I don’t eat them on their own first, then I mix them together along with a little balsamic vinegar (and some fresh herbs like basil) to make a delicious and healthy summer salad.

DXNBhzRFU6m.content:

Karen Blaedow is a Horticultural Agent at NC Cooperative Extension we are excited for her to bring her expertise and connections to our mission. We asked her a little about herself and this is what she had to say!

Q: What are you up to when you’re not at our board meetings? 
A:  When I am not at ASAP board meetings, I’m working full-time assisting vegetable and small fruit farms in Henderson County. I also currently serve on a few additional boards which include the NC Tomato Growers Association, North American Raspberry and Blackberry Association, NC Caneberry Association and as the chair of the WNC AgOptions Steering Committee. When I’m not working, I’m gardening, immersing myself in nature and spending lots of time with my husband and son.

Q: Why is ASAP important to you?
A: ASAP has played a critical role in the work that I do with local foods and in particular farmers markets. I can’t think of a more impactful partner organization working in this space. ASAP provides community support for helping producers market their local products, they empower markets to provide a place for local farms to sell their products and more importantly their programs help increase local food access to more customers regardless of their economic situation. ASAP builds farms, markets & community!

Q: What’s your favorite local food dish? 
A: I’m a mushroom maniac so basically any dish that has oysters, maitake, or lion’s mane with it.

DYQL8GxnDc2.content:
Food informs our identities—it holds our history, our present time, and our future. It’s no secret that the Southern Appalachian region has a long and rich history of traditional foods with strong ties to the land. Appalachian people are known for using what they have. Characterized by food preservation, game meat, and foraging, Appalachian food traditions were born out of geographic isolation, resourcefulness through poverty, farming ingenuity among mountain landscapes, and strong ties to community.

In this year’s Local Food Guide, we share stories from farmers about their ties to Southern Appalachian foodways. Read about how tobacco shaped our region, how farmers like @burnettefamilyfarm are keeping sorghum alive, why @blackthornfarmandkitchen is growing out a productive pawpaw orchard, and the reasons @melvinhillmeats is raising the heritage American Guinea hog.

Read more of these stories at asapconnections.org/guide, or look for the print edition, available for free at farmers markets, local businesses, and other community locations over the coming weeks.

Photo 2 by @micahusher 
Photo 3 & 4 by @hello_my_name_is_stephanie

ASAP's Local Food Research Center annually surveys farmers in the Appalachian Grown region to assess changes and opportunities in the local food system. A report based on the 2025 Appalachian Grown Producer Survey is available now at asapconnections.org/research-reports.

Analysis of the annual survey data, which includes questions about land access, production costs, market opportunities, marketing strategies, and product sales, helps inform ASAP’s farmer programs. The 2025 survey was completed approximately 14 months after Hurricane Helene struck the region and in addition to standard questions farmers were asked about the impact the year after the storm.

Despite hardships brought about by Helene and economic instability due to national and global factors, Appalachian Grown farmers remained hopeful with many citing the power of community support. Read more in the report.

DYh-N19kjJ0.content:
This year, students across North Carolina will eat locally grown products in school meals, engage in educational activities about agriculture and nutrition, and take part in school gardening experiences. 

According to the 2023 USDA Farm to School Census, 59 percent of school nutrition departments in North Carolina served local foods in their schools, ranking 34th out of 50 states, and 10 percent of total food costs came from local products, ranking 41st out of 50 states.

School nutrition directors often want to purchase more local products, and farmers often want to sell to local school districts, but challenges to purchasing local food remain.

In this year’s Local Food Guide, we feature the momentum and challenges behind local food in schools. This story is excerpted from the original by Analisa Sorrells Archer with @educationnc. Find the full text at ednc.org/schools-want-to-serve-more-local-food-in-cafeterias-but-challenges-remain.

Read more of these stories at asapconnections.org/guide, or look for the print edition, available for free at farmers markets, local businesses, and other community locations over the coming weeks.

asapconnections.historical_summary:

The writing frequently uses clear instructions, links, tagged partners, and occasional emojis or hashtags to encourage readers to sign up for CSAs, visit markets, attend events, apply for opportunities, donate or support local food access, and explore resources. The overall emotional tendency is positive, hopeful, and community-centered, emphasizing sustainability, local food access, and connections among farmers, consumers, schools, and organizations.
Accounts this user follows often involve small-scale agriculture, specialty food production, and local market-oriented food businesses.

DBc2tbzxOFI.content:
Helene washed away so much precious topsoil from WNC farms. We’re brainstorming ways to rebuild and remediate the soil with mushrooms.

Last year, we partnered with the SAHC incubator farm to begin trials for a mushroom compost operation using our spent growing medium. Pictured here is the compost after one year of passive decomposition. 

I’m currently writing a SARE grant to use stropharia and oyster mushrooms to speed decomposition of woody debris left by the storm. Inoculated mulch from downed trees could be used to add organic material back to fields relatively quickly. I’m looking for a few partner farms to include in this SARE grant. Please reach out if you’re interested!

Beyond the accelerated debris cleanup and soil building aspects of this preliminary project, I’d like to determine if our mushroom compost can truly boost microbial life in flood depleted soils by “seeding” the soil with mycelium and improving soil structure.

And lastly, I’d like to explore the purported remediation properties of oyster mushrooms. Mycoremediation is a newer and less studied field than phytoremediation. Many bold claims have been made that mushrooms can save the world. But we need much more detail and scientific work to back up these claims! I wasn’t sure what my academic future held after completing my MS this spring, but now my path seems more clear. Please reach out if you’re interested in these projects too, I’d love to collaborate!

#mountainstrong #hurricanehelene #mushroomfarm #soilhealth #mycoremediation

DJu6wrVxevY.content:
Massospora cicidina

So stoked to find some of these this year!
This fungus infects only 13 and 17 year cicadas. Nymphs are infected by spores in the soil as they climb their way to the surface. The fungus then takes over their body and they develop a plug of spores where their lower abdomen used to be!
The cicadas then fly and crawl around spreading spores over every surface for the next generation. 
The fungus supplies them with amphet@mines to keep them going and attempting to mate with other cicadas. 

This one was found amongst at least half a dozen others dying on the sidewalk in north Asheville. 
.
.
.
#massosporacicadina #cicadas #entomopathogenicfungi

Soooo funny story.
Preface: we’re deeply grateful for what we have and know there’s a lot of heavy stuff happening in the world but this weekend at the farm was a comedy of errors.

Saturday morning I broke my right hand sledding down the neighborhood hill. Haven’t seen a doctor yet because urgent cares were closed, we don’t have a 4WD family car, and the toddler can’t ride in the truck 🙃 Ortho appointment today 🤞

Meanwhile Jay spent the morning thawing HVAC drain lines in the mushroom building using a hairdryer, a lighter, and a tea kettle. He’s still running around trying to save fruiting rooms that froze overnight.

I did animal chores left-handed and repurposed the broken sled to haul hay to the donkeys while Grandma watched Wren on FaceTime because school’s canceled.

It’s one of those stretches where the all-work-no-play life is getting to us. I’m grateful to be in control of our work and to contribute to local food production, but also feeling very worn down and not totally sure how I’m about to parent a toddler with one hand 🫠

C4RE5VYsu4E.content:
When I met a friend yesterday, she and her talked about being self-employed or even entrepreneurs as women* and and how it is like, to be frequently underestimated, frequently assumed that there has to be a „partner“ doing this with us, the expectations being higher in so many situations as if we were men leading a company and at the same time basically handling our struggles alone most of the time, because if you have a look around… mostly, in our position, it’s men. It still is. I sometimes forget this because I work with almost only self-employed women around me. But actual… that’s pretty rare. 

And it got clear to me again that even now that I’ve built and working in a studio almost completely run by women, I can’t escape being put in a role, or making assumptions or being tried to be exploited just because I’m female passing in so many situations. 

Best example: hiring handymen for studio renovations. I went from being nice to being not really nice anymore because chances are super high someone tries to rip me off if I’m just nice to them. 

Can we just stop doing this? Start seeing people as people, treating everyone with respect, start giving everyone the same chances… can’t be so hard? Why do we still have to fight for these things? 

At the same time I’m thankful that my problems are „only“ this where I live, that people can go on the street here and that we have come a long way. My thoughts go out to all women* on earth who still have to fight for their basic human rights in their lives. 

I hope you had a good day everyone 🤍

C8RaRbpsuyP.content:
„Aber es ist doch ‚nur‘ eine Linie?!“ bekomme ich öfter mal als Reaktion nach einer Anfrage auf mein Angebot. Da blutet mir immer etwas das Herz, denn gerade perfekte Linien und Ringe stellen mit das Anspruchsvollste dar, was man sich tätowieren lassen kann. 

Daher nehme ich euch heute mal mit durch einen Termin! Zuerst zeichne ich die Linie in mehreren Gängen Freihand an, um eine möglichst genaue Vorlage zu erzielen. Ich arbeite hier ohne Stencil, was ein in meinen Augen noch besseres Ergebnis erzielt und eventuelle Ecken durchs Anlegen vermeidet. 

Danach tätowiere ich ganz vorsichtig die Linie und arbeite mich auch hier vorsichtig in meist mehreren Durchgängen nach vorne. Ich sag’s euch wie es ist, in den ersten Jahren meiner Karriere hatte ich vor solchen Tagen echt schlaflose Nächte. Denn was wäre schlimmer, wenn man eine gerade Linie anfragt und am Ende eine Sinuskurve am Arm hat? (Nothing personal Sinuskurven, ihr seid super 😄)

Nun, nach 8 Jahren tätowieren, bringe ich so viel Routine mit, dass mir diese Termine immer leichter von der Hand gehen und allgemein liebe ich ja eh die Herausforderung, Dinge möglichst perfekt zu machen ;) bedenkt also, dass wenn ihr ein Motiv wie dieses anfragt, ihr auch und vor allem für die Jahre an Lernen,  Expertise und die ruhige Hand bezahlt, die es benötigt, es am Ende so clean und simpel aussehen zu lassen. 

Habt ihr Fragen zu Lines oder Ringen oder habt ihr Interesse an einem ähnlichen Motiv? Schreibt sie mir in die Kommentare oder sendet mir eine Anfrage an daniela@sweetbabysunshine.com!

Und übrigens, was haltet ihr davon, wenn ich die Texte hier ab jetzt auf deutsch schreibe?

DPjeWTiiOiY.content:
Hatte diese Serie schon länger in meinen Zeichnungen. Ich könnt jedes der Ornamente anfragen.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Heute fühle ich mich nur noch selten so, und wenn ich bedenke, dass ich mich letztes Jahr zu dieser Zeit noch in der Tagesklinik befunden habe kann ich mittlerweile sagen, dass ich einen echt weiten Weg gekommen bin. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
In der Klinik erhielt ich die Diagnose Borderline und plötzlich ergab vieles Sinn. Gleichzeitig wusste ich eigentlich rein garnichts darüber, hatte nur Vorurteile in meinem Kopf von manipulativen, toxischen „Monstern“, die Menschen verletzen und die so quasi der Antichrist der psychischen Störungen seien. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Mittlerweile verstehe ich die Krankheit besser und weiß, dass das natürlich ziemlich an der Realität vorbeigeht. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Denn eigentlich ist die tragische Ironie an der Krankheit, dass zwischenmenschliche Connection, Liebe, Geborgenheit, also Dinge die Menschen zum (Über)leben benötigen, uns als Kind genommen oder nie mitgegeben wurden. Das, was wir uns am allermeisten auf der Welt wünschen, ist gleichzeitig auch das, was uns am allermeisten Angst macht. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
So jagen wir etwas hinterher, das wir uns so sehnlichst und verzweifelt wünschen, und wenn wir es bekommen, halten wir es nicht aus. Oder Kappen Bindungen, aus Angst verlassen zu werden, verletzen uns auf verschiedenste Weisen selber, gehen ausbeuterische Beziehungen ein um ein Stück Liebe zu bekommen, leben in einem ständigen Alarmzustand der Gefühle. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Es ist wirklich ein harter Kampf, Heilung zu erreichen. Borderline gilt als die am schmerzhaftesten zu ertragende psychische Krankheit mit der höchsten Su*z*drate.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
Aber, und das geht gerade an dich solltest du auch die Diagnose haben: die Krankheit ist keine Endstation. Mit den richtigen Maßnahmen wird es besser! Therapien, sich Informieren und Selbsthilfegruppen, Wahrnehmung und Akzeptanz der eigenen Gefühle, sowie Arbeiten am Selbstwert haben mir extrem geholfen. 
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

In 2024, Inkblot Studio partnered with Dog-Eared Books to run a fundraiser to combat book banning in Iowa. We had so much fun that we’re back, better than ever, and have more artists donating their time and talents to raise money for reproductive healthcare access in Iowa. 

Designs are repeatable, and cost from $60-$150 dollars donated to one of the selected organizations. Tipping your artist is appreciated.

Inkblot Studio and artists at Heroic Ink have created a selection of walk-in tattoo designs. However, the flash tattoo event is about more than just getting inked: it’s about fighting for equitable access to reproductive healthcare in the state that we call home. 

For those who would like to donate and participate but don’t want the commitment of a permanent tattoo, we will have stickers available at the store, from which proceeds will be donated to the listed organizations. 

Tattoos are first come, first serve. Participants must be 18+. 

 

Need something to do while you’re waiting for your tattoo? Family Planning Council of Iowa will be at Dog-Eared Books hosting a letter-writing campaign to remind our representatives what Iowans really want: fair, equitable access to reproductive healthcare. 

Check our social media for a sneak peak of designs!

PARTICIPANTS MUST LINE UP AT THE TATTOO SHOP THAT HAS THEIR PREFERRED ARTIST. Both shops are on the 200 block of Main Street, on the north side.

❗It is past time that we tell y'all more about our incredible Chef Brooke Adams (she/they).

For 11+ years, Brooke has worked across the Asheville food scene, receiving mentorship from beloved chefs like Terri Terrell of Homegrown and Utopian Seed, Luis Martinez of Tequio Foods, and Michelle Bailey of Smokey Park Supper Club.

They cut their teeth as sous chef to Eric Morris at the Funkatorium & Cultura, helping earn Cultura a spot as a semifinalist in the James Beard Foundation's Best New Restaurant category. Around Helene, Brooke transitioned to the team run by their work wife, Mallory Foster, now Executive Chef at Rhubarb. Brooke chose to leave finer dining for Finest to focus on food that their farmer partners can afford to eat regularly.

Brooke grew up in these mountains in a family of restaurant people, and they’ve stayed in WNC to build a life with their wife and four(!) dogs. They found a second home in the kitchen, among other (self-described) misfits working towards a common goal. Brooke cooks to make people try things they’ve never had or think they won’t like. And they became a chef because they are a leader who invests in the growth of everyone around them. Both of these miracles happen at Finest every single day!

Hopefully next time you eat at Finest, you'll notice Brooke's unique touch; from lunch specials to cozy handmade pastas to fresh market salads, their focus on seasonality, commitment to using the whole plant/animal, and  talent for balancing flavors and textures always shine through. ✨

We love you Brooke and we are so grateful for you!

DF_btFuRAZl.content:
Hi friends! Just wanted to do a reintroduction post with the fresh flower season getting ready to kick off next month!
.
My name is Sara (she/her) and I run Freckle Twins' Garden under the strict supervision of the Freckle Twins, Max and Mochi. With a bit of help from my husband, @gregorielrobles . (We will be celebrating our 10th wedding anniversary this August)!
.
We moved to Waynesville in 2022, closing on the farm that April. That first season, I grew almost 100 dahlias in grow bags and sold them to local florists while we worked on building the raised beds in what is now our flower field. 
.
Since then, we've grown thousands of flowers without any chemical inputs or ever utilizing a tiller. 
.
In the years leading up to us buying the farm, I worked on other farms, started a market garden (Freckle Twins' Garden 1.0), attended seminars and conferences and classes, read all the books, listened to all the podcasts, and all in all just tried to absorb AALLL the information. I still do. 
.
In all that learning and all that trial and error, I fell in love with the concept of sustainable agriculture. Sustainable for the environment, and sustainable for the people involved. Working with nature instead of against, and working with my disabilities rather than against them. 
.
I love sharing the information I've learned over the years with anyone and everyone who will listen (I'm really exciting at dinner parties since all I want to talk about is vermicomposting and regionally adapted land race seed trials). I believe with enough determination and patience, anyone can have a green thumb. You just might want to have a good composting system set up first to recycle all the plants you're going to kill. 🤪
.
We are members of the Diversity Business Directory through @ideaofhaywood because we welcome marginalized communities with open arms. 
.
So with every flower purchase, you can rest assured they are 100% chemical free, local (my front yard), and supporting a dream of sharing these beautiful, high quality flowers with the world. 
.

Hi friends!

I'm now in my second semester of grad school at NC State. I've been taking A full time course load, so I should actually be done with the class requirements by the end of this year, but my research requirements won't be finished until next year.

So for the foreseeable future, I will be living and breathing school. What does this mean for the farm? I'm so glad you asked. 

We've shifted from a for-profit business to a homestead mindset. 

There are still thousands of daffodils, dozens of peonies, and hundreds of dahlias in the ground, plus all sorts of volunteers that always pop up. I plan to still offer these easy perennial beauties to you all since the only work I have to do is post and harvest. So, I'll be shifting this page away from 100% flowers and towards what I'm working on/learning, what brings me joy, AND flowers. So school, gardening, books, my art, the dogs, and flowers. How does that sound?

DVJkqAfDnRG.content:
Some days before getting started on school work I like to wake up my brain with a quick painting. Today that looked like messy mark making. No structure, no rhyme or reason, just making marks on the page and letting my brain relax.
.
I've never actually used these watercolor crayons before in a painting. They were gifted to me when I was 9 by a professional watercolorist who took a shine to me when I met her. All I remember of her is the impression of her being short and petite with snow white hair and a no-nonsense countenance. The other thing I remember is how every wall in her home was covered in artwork. I was spellbound by how she captured the heart of the Everglades (we lived in Florida then), the feeling that she had pinned the souls of animals to paper. The egrets, the manatees, the alligators, all seemingly pinned to the walls like butterflies in a shadow box. I don't know how long the grownups spoke, but I was not ready to leave when the time came. I wanted to wander the wilderness of my home in her home forever. She pressed this tin of watercolor crayons and a small travel palette of watercolors into my hands before we left. 
.
The travel palette was lost in one of my many moves over the years, but the crayons remain. I didn't start my watercolor journey until just a few years ago in 2022. The crayons don't work as well as I'm sure they did when they were fresh and new, but the feeling of fated inevitably clings to them. So I'll hold onto them for the memory and as a pseudo museum piece of foreshadowing in my life.
.
Do you have anything like this that feels like a piece of foreshadowing from when you were younger? 
.
#watercolours #watercolorsketchbook #memories #watercolorcrayons #arttherapy

DWg036iliUQ.content:
it feels weird to release my #hcloutattoos march flash drop when community members are STILL experiencing the negative impacts of operation metro surge and the federal occupation of ice/dhs/bp. 

but in this timeline, capitalism is still a thing. and in this timeline (and all), i urge you to support small, local, bipoc, queer, fat, immigrant, gender expansive, disabled, and minoritized businesses. we need your support to continue to survive and thrive! 

you can still support my community by booking mutual aid tattoos! flash tattoos will still benefit canmn and east saint paul rental assistance and can be scheduled through the end of may. 50% of each tattoo will go to indigenous roots for rental assistance for housing and small businesses. 

since early february, $10,080 has been donated to indigenous roots for rent assistance! $5697.75 has been donated to canmn since mid january! $530 has been redistributed to other renters who needed support as well. wow! 

you can make a tattoo appointment with me at calendly.com/hclou or you can message me! 

 1. check out the design drop for this month. if you like one, book via my calendly in my profile. there is a $50 non-refundable deposit for non-patreon members. 

2. i’m currently booking for may - july at cozy camp collective! 

3. my rates are sliding scale: $140-$185/hour for bipoc clients. $165-$200/hour for all other clients. 

4. i prefer some color in the design, but/and am open black/gray! all colors on flash sheets are suggestions, you pick what works for you! smaller tattoos will be no smaller than 2.5-3 inches! larger tattoos will be no smaller than 5 inches. tattoos are repeatable 2x and then retired. 

5. i’m taking custom requests for full color pet portraits, line work pet portraits, funfetti filler designs, food, cover-ups, scar cover ups, florals, and other designs by request. customs have a one time $100 drawing fee. 

6. other designs from previous months are still available! check out my highlights or pinned posts for previous designs. 

7. any questions? just ask. excited to see you in my chair soon!

xoxox.

This account primarily shares colorful tattoo work, digital art, pet portraits, zines/exhibits, and mutual-aid updates, especially in Minnesota. The writing is casual, lowercase, playful, and emotionally direct, mixing affectionate humor, political anger, gratitude, and community care. Posts advocate anti-racist, pro-immigrant, survivor-support, housing, and mental-health causes while celebrating dogs, family, ancestors, and small businesses. Interaction preferences include tagging clients and collaborators, sharing booking instructions via Calendly/DM, asking followers to tag public officials, promoting flash drops and donation rates, and inviting questions or community support.
Accounts this user follows often involve tattoo studio practices centered on consent, client comfort, and ethical body art.

hera.ttt.historical_summary: The user posts mainly about anime, manga, and gaming-inspired tattoos, including works from Avatar: The Last Airbender, Studio Ghibli, Jujutsu Kaisen, Demon Slayer, Chainsaw Man, Cyberpunk 2077, and Naruto, often as a Vienna-based tattoo apprentice working at True Canvas. The writing style is casual, playful, and emoji-rich, with frequent hashtags, short captions, quoted lines, and behind-the-scenes notes about sessions, custom designs, healed pieces, and booking availability. The emotional tone is warm, grateful, excited, and reflective, emphasizing client trust, milestones, and love for fandom culture. Interaction preferences include thanking clients, tagging collaborators, inviting bookings via bio links, asking followers to guess anime or manga, and sharing both finished work and imperfect or off-grid pieces.

C0h6pSxpKJ9.content:
Of all of the healing modalities and practices and tools and books and ceremonies I’ve done, one of the most truly life changing has been the practice of sauna/cold plunge. When I say it changed my life, I mean it literally changed my life by changing my nervous system. 🥹

I started doing this practice over four years ago hoping to help my ptsd symptoms and have been consistent with it ever since.. on the low side, 1-2 days per week and on the higher, 5-7 days per week. I do around 15 minutes of sauna and 1-3 minutes of cold plunge (honoring my cycle & listening to my body). 

Putting your body in a controlled “stressful” environment is a tool that allows you to train your nervous system to become better able to adapt to stress and triggers. 
When you enter the cold, your nervous system initially wants to freak out.. to put it simply, the nervous system interprets this as “I’m dying”. But in that moment, when you choose to not listen to that, to not go down the path of freaking out, you can actually go deeper and deeper into the peaceful state that ALWAYS exists within.. you find your breath and your center and then it becomes actually amazingly enjoyable.

Because of this practice, I would notice that loud noises wouldn’t jolt me, or my daughter having a big emotion didn’t take me with her… I can be the rock to hold it all.. I can handle discomfort. And I even find in actually stressful and big triggering moments, I can so easily find my peace - truly thanks to this practice. 🥹

Of course there are tons of other benefits to sauna and cold plunge that I’ll let you find on your own but this is my experience and it has been so profound that I hope many others will find inspiration to try it.

I am so grateful for the beautiful space of Drip Sauna here in Asheville. My new friends, the owners, Daniel and Evan are incredible guys with a beautiful passion for the tradition of sauna and cold plunge and they could not have done a better job creating an absolutely stunning space to experience it. From the lights, to the fire, right by the river… and to the gratitude and prayers they have spoken over the space. Everything about it feels nourishing and healing. 

Cont….

C1sq0lZImbN.content:
I’ve never had a reaction so strong to someone in my entire life.. it felt similar to turning two magnetics the opposing way and trying to press them together. A force demanding me to distance myself from him. I was disgusted by him the second I met him and I knew nothing about him.

My body knew. 

Later I would be told by a friend that “he’s actually really great…” and in that moment, I listened to someone else and denied my own body.. my intuition. This decision would result in the worst kind of abuse I could ever imagine. 

Have you ever had a strong body reaction to someone? Did you listen?

The body always knows.

Even if it doesn’t make sense, please listen. 

You can trust your body. 

And the deeper and deeper we go into this work, the louder it becomes. 

This is your compass loves. 💗 

If you’re not sure how to find that voice, let’s talk. I’m here to support you!

C4WmL4oJfJE.content:
This is something that can truly save you from more unnecessary pain or cause you to be stuck in a challenging time for longer than you need to be.

•Be Aware of the Vultures.•

Thinking about our feathery cleanup friends, the vultures… they show up for what’s dying/dead.. it feeds them!

The concept of vultures as it relates to people and trauma is that theee are people who quite literally do the same.. they flock to the “dying” or the trauma energy.

Those who have not yet healed their own trauma and nervous system can often be addicted to drama. They can be addicted to pain and things that bring their nervous system back into a triggered state because they have become so used to it. 

I have noticed this in the past and thankfully had this awareness last year moving through my own major life challenge. 

Having this awareness made me hyper sensitive to how certain people would act around me and the ones who seemed to just show up for the drama and “excitement”, yet were no where to be found in the extremely dark long days (when I actually needed the support).

The reason this can cause a lot more harm to an already challenging situation is because:

1 - it keeps you in the drama loop.. going over and over the same pain story and adding someone else’s triggered nervous system to it does not serve you. 

2 - it does not inspire you to make the changes you might need to in order to move through the painful situation 

3 - and because of that, it can keep you stuck in the loop of the trauma and make it near impossible to get out 

(Repeating the cycle)

C48a-iAuVQ4.content:
This has come up a lot for my clients recently with the lunar eclipse (she is a beautiful Teacher and here to bring up what’s in the shadow😅) so I thought I would share and hope this can be helpful for someone out there. 🥰✨

When an old wound or story comes up *again*, it is completely valid to feel frustrated, disempowered, even angry.. we might want to quickly shut it down and invalidate it because “I’ve already healed that”😤. 

But I’d like to invite you to try a practice the next time this happens.

Rather than seeing this wound or story coming up as YOU, I want you to see this as one PART of you. 

This is a single part of the beautiful kaleidoscope of you.

When we see it as one part, we can much more easily accept it and move through it from an empowered place.

And often these stories or wounds don’t make complete sense for the situation now.. but they do make perfect sense for this living part of you that experienced everything he/she did. And the truth is, if it’s still coming up, it needs to be loved, validated, and befriended.

The urge to shut it down really only serves to keep this wound growing mold in the closet. 😢 we might think if it’s quiet, it’s healed… until it comes out again in an explosive trigger moment.

So rather than shutting it down, we acknowledge this one part of us and treat it as alive and valid (because it is!).

Disempowered and Invalidating Mindset
❌ I should be over this 
❌I already did the work on this
❌This is so silly

Empowered and Validating Mindset
✅I see this part of me and it’s valid that it’s here
✅I’m sorry you did not feel safe at one point, you’re safe now. I’ve got you.
✅I love you. I see you. Thank you. 
✅I will keep you safe now. Is there more? 

It’s quite powerful to be able to see these waves that come through as parts of us and not US. This is a place of empowerment where you get to now be the older, wiser self, validating the story and the wound in the way that you always deserved. And truly, this is how deeper healing and integration happens. 🥰🥰

There is not a single part of you that is not worthy of being seen and loved.

I hope you’ll try this and I hope its helpful.🥰💗✨
Jess🌹

C4_FVyQuoRa.content:

Just as I’ve called on the strength of my ancestors and felt them rejoicing with me for saying ENOUGH..

C5j5drjJv4c.content:
This is something that has come up a lot for my single female clients lately.. and it’s something that can truly save you so much unnecessary heartache. 

Here is a hard truth….😅

If a healthy masculine man is interested in you, he will come to you. He will tell you, he will come to see you, he will ask you out… you will know.
The only thing you should be doing, is softening and opening to him. 

It’s amazing to me witnessing my clients experience this for the first time.. there is a lot of fear that comes up in the waiting .. “what if he doesn’t reach out again..?” And the work is in sitting with the feelings that come up around it.. because whether he does or doesn’t, you choosing to wait will make sure that you don’t end up with someone who didn’t actually want you or wasn’t ready for you!

You see, men are biologically programmed to go after what they want… in fact, this brings them great joy..😍

Obviously this does not apply to every single man, as humans are all unique and beautiful in their own way. 

But for most men, it is true!

So if he is not pursuing you in the way you desire, he is most likely either not that interested or quite honestly he is not ready… because when he has done his own inner work and can feel proud of who he is when he rises to pursue you, you will have total clarity in how this man feels about you. He is sure of himself and he is sure of you. 

And until then, make the commitment to yourself that you won’t force another relationship ever again. 

When you start to take on the role of pursuer, what happens is most likely you will end up with a man who either didn’t really want you or wasn’t ready for you! And quite possibly end up in the more masculine role in the relationship (not attractive to anyone). None of which create a loving and healthy relationship… and often both result in your own pain.

But the beautiful thing is, for the healthy masculine who is ready for you, you won’t have to control, nag, or beg for his attention..

Keep focusing your beautiful energy on you.. do your own work to make sure that your heart is wide open, give him the invitation, and watch the right man rise to be the King you deserve. 😍🔥

C5oJCUDOUwY.content:
One of my clients was SHOCKED when I told her I will never ever speak badly about myself…

It has become so normalized in our society to bash ourselves, and judge every inch of ourselves, that it is literally shocking when someone doesn’t do that… 

But have you ever considered that somewhere in there, you became your own bully?😥🥺

There is so much NOISE about how we should look, how we should dress, how we should act, how we should talk…. The “bullying” is everywhere, why do we do it to ourselves too?

I remember in high school, I had amazing friends… and… I was also fairly frequently teased for “always being happy”… I was teased for having a bubbly personality, for exploding with joy when I was excited, for being expressive in my tone and how I spoke… 

And you know what I did? I quite literally changed myself… I lowered my speaking voice, I held back excitement, and I tried to act less happy…. How wild is that? 

It took years of inner work and putting in time with my self-love practices… I learned to fall in love with all of the things that make me, me! I retrained my mind to LOVE those special things about me..
I would get excited and jump up and down, and then say to myself “ I love how excited you get, it’s so cute when you get so excited!” 🥹🥹
And the healing happened..
It doesn’t happen overnight but a really good start is just making a promise to yourself..

I WILL NOT BE MY OWN BULLY. 

And when you notice those thoughts coming up, judging yourself, your body, your voice, your anything, you pause… you notice it… and you change it to… “I LOVE ……” whatever the thing is.

I spent hours sitting in front of a mirror looking at my “flaws” and saying I LOVE YOU to everyone of them until my curves became something  I didn’t hate but actually I felt sexy for.😊

So again, it doesn’t happen overnight but this is some of the most important work we can do… especially as women - with the insane standards put on us before we even hit puberty… 
When we show up to love ourselves deeply and truly, we give others permission to do the same. And I truly believe the world would be a totally different place if we all learned how to love ourselves. 

Will you join me?

C6rKQB1O5ab.content:
When I was a kid, I printed out my favorite quotes and taped them all around the walls in my bedroom…

(It’s funny to think about this now that it’s a trendy thing to do…)

I remember one of them was a John Lennon quote that said.. 
Everything will be okay in the end… if it’s not okay, it’s not the end.🥹

Sometimes we can get so caught up in what life is moving us through that it’s very hard to see outside of this moment. It feels as if we are tumbling under a massive wave and can’t come up for air… surely this is it, right?

It’s not… 

And the truth is, we don’t want to NOT go through this hard stuff because then there would be no growth. The hardest things we’ve ever gone through all have one thing in common - they pushed us to grow and they propelled us to the next level in life. 

Trust me, you do not want to NOT go through the hard times.

So when we can remind ourselves in the thick of the storm, even if just for a moment, to pause and look from a higher perspective, this moment is really just one blip in the span of your life. And it will pass. 💗

Some of my favorite affirmations “in the storm” are..
“I trust my path”
“Thank you for these lessons”
“Thank you for this growth” 

So if you’re in that hard moment in your life where you feel as if you’re being tossed around by the waves of life, just know that this is not the end. You cannot even imagine yet how good life is going to be on the other side of this. And if I can support you, I’m here! 💗

C9LGP-VJDOq.content:
The next time you find yourself worked up over an old trauma, something you feel you’ve done “the work” to heal, and you start getting frustrated that it’s coming up again…. 😔😤

I want you to try this.😍

Try to think of this as one PART of beautiful you. The part of you getting triggered is not YOU, it’s one part of you and the version of you that lived through this big and potentially horrible experience. 

This part “coming up” doesn’t mean that you aren’t healed and it does NOT mean that you are any less lovable!

These hurt parts of us can be triggered by so many things - someone’s tone of voice, a smell, a sound… but whatever it is, this part of you is coming up to be seen and accepted. It’s coming up because it feels safe to do so. And by seeing it as one part of you, it’s much easier to then have compassion and love for this part.

Because guess what… all of that work you have done means that there is another part of you that is more healed and wiser and who can hold this other part with love. 😍💗

This is how you become your own healer and the one you have always needed!

Once you can do this, the more healed parts of you get to say to this other part, “I see you.. it’s valid that you’re here. You’re safe here, I’ve got you! I love and accept you!” 

And the beauty of this, is often that’s exactly what this part needs to fully integrate and no longer “come up”. 

This is the exact type of thing I teach my clients everyday and I hope it can be helpful for someone reading this. 🥰

C9NKJ4nuxZ-.content:
What you resist, persists.. 💗

(A follow-up to my last share)

When we try to deny, shame, avoid, and shut down our emotions or any ‘part’ of us, we may think it just goes away. But the truth is, it is basically the same as shoving an old sandwich in a closet… the mold grows. 😳

Emotions that are unfelt and parts of us that we do not accept about ourselves grow and become dis-ease in our body. This one thing we thought wasn’t a big deal or we shouldn’t be upset about, can actually lead to physical and mental health issues. This is the actual manifestation of the unfelt emotion. 😢

So if you want to know how to feel the most free, alive, and happy in this life? 

Let yourself feel it all. Accept it all. And LOVE it all. 

And if you’re not sure how to do that or are scared to start (what if I can’t stop - is a common question I get), please reach out. I help my clients through this work and to the other side of freedom every single day. 😍🔥

You are beautifully human and that means all aspects of human emotions exist and are beautiful within you. 🥰😍

DAB5pyMS4A_.content:
Learn to Sit With Big Emotions - Change Your Life 😍

When someone is sitting in front of you and feeling something BIG, do you get triggered? Do you get uncomfortable?
If your child is crying and screaming, does that infuriate you and cause you to react?

So many of us were never taught this incredibly important and valuable skill - emotion regulation. 

The truth is, if we don’t know how to do this for our own SELF, it will be incredibly difficult to do it for the person in front of us - no matter how much we love them. 🥹

Something you’ll hear me say a lot in my work is that it HAS to always start with ME. Your work always has to start with YOU. 

When you can become totally comfortable with your own emotions and learn healthy ways to express them, you will be able to hold that same loving, grounded space for the person in front of you!

DCj9tg8yqx9.content:
On days when you are feeling under-resourced, it is perfectly normal to feel extra sensitive… 

This might be from not enough sleep/rest, a lack of nutritious foods, dehydrated, not enough time outside, or too much time away from community, as some examples… 

What we resist persists - rather than should-ing all over yourself, “I should feel better”, “I should do more before I pause”, I want to encourage you to slow down, pause and turn to some practices that can help soothe your nervous system before it becomes a much bigger issue. 

Some of my favorite practices for when I am under-resourced:

•A barefoot walk in nature
•Sun on my skin
•Humming (helps to regulate the nervous system)
•Slow breaths in for 4 and out for 8 (or more) - turns on parasympathetic nervous system 
•Big glass of water
•Tulsi Ashwaganda Tea
•HerbPharm Tinctures (many blends - all amazing)
•Affirmations - “I am safe”, “this is just a season”, “it’s okay that I’m feeling sensitive” 
•Holding just above my earlobes and pulling down about 8-10 times.. continuing until I feel calm.

The reason I am so deeply passionate about the work that I do is because I use it everyday and it WORKS. Life is tough sometimes and we can never avoid that… but we can absolutely learn and practice skills that will allow us to move through the tough times and be okay (or better than okay!!!) in the midst of them. 

If you could use support through a tough time, or just know that you’re ready for deep healing, personal development and growth, please reach out! I currently have space available for 3 or 6-month 1:1 containers.🌹

CI9FPsKlwzi.content:
“The Realm of Hogwarts Castle and the Forbidden Forest”. 

Finally Completed last night. 

Done in about 120 hours and shaded with dotwork. Jessie let me wonder about the forest to find my own path to completion exploring as far as I could before finally wandering out and glancing back. I am soo grateful for the chance to spend 6+ hours in palm size areas session by session and then step back and see the entirety of the Realm appear in full capacity. 

The coolest part about this piece to me is the spiders. I wanted to give ALL of my coworkers the ability to freehand a random spider into the forest to incorporate a piece of their souls take on the personality of their spider, and then after I tattooed it. kirioustattoos.historical_summary: Kerri Kiple’s posts are mainly tattoo-artist portfolio updates, covering new work, healed tattoos, cover-ups, flash events, client shoutouts, and occasional paintings or drawings. The content highlights colorful and black-and-grey tattoo subjects such as flowers, animals, insects, sea creatures, anime/pop-culture designs, memorial pieces, and small personal concepts. Her writing style is casual, enthusiastic, and friendly, using short captions, playful phrases, emojis, and many hashtags for location, shop, style, and subject tags. Emotionally, the posts are mostly positive, grateful, and excited, with a few tender or sentimental moments around memorial tattoos and healed work. She prefers interacting through tagging clients and fellow artists, thanking people, inviting bookings via email or link, and encouraging followers to swipe for close-ups or before-and-after details.

korelrivera.historical_summary: Korel’s posts mainly document commissioned graffiti murals, street-art collaborations, exhibitions, travel, and tattoo work, especially in Japan and the Netherlands with strong Mexican cultural references such as lucha libre, boxing, Day of the Dead, and Mexican art. The writing is informal, enthusiastic, and community-focused, often using emojis, many hashtags, multilingual snippets, and direct invitations to events or bookings. Emotionally, the posts are positive and grateful, emphasizing pride in projects, friendships, and new opportunities. Interaction preferences include tagging collaborators, studios, venues, photographers, and clients; reposting event announcements; and encouraging followers to visit, share, or contact him for mural and tattoo commissions.

DXXhznRyZsk.content:
One day when I’m gone, it brings me so much happiness that little pieces of me will be cherished and loved on others bodies forever🥹💖✨
Tattooing is a deeply personal energy exchange between two people. I don’t take this responsibility lightly. 
Every tattoo I have on my body I remember the session. I might not remember all the words that were said but I remember the feeling of our time spent together. Some good, some bad. And I’m reminded of those feelings when I look at my tattoos. 
I knew when I stepped into this industry that one of my main goals was to provide a safe and inclusive space for my clients. I not only want to give people a piece of artwork that will love flower, but the feeling of being safe with me. 💖

DOlfdU_De1n.content:
Vor drei Jahren war da dieses Gefühl von Ohnmacht, Wut und Trauer – nach der Katastrophe vor Griechenland, als an einem einzigen Tag über 600 Menschen im Mittelmeer ertrinken mussten.

Aus einer kleinen Idee – ein paar Soli-Tattoos für die zivile Seenotrettung @seawatchcrew – ist seitdem etwas Großes geworden: @inkagainstborders 
Eine Bewegung, die inzwischen jedes Jahr dutzende FLINTA*-Artists, Merch, Rahmenprogramm und unendlich viel Solidarität zusammenbringt.

Ich bin so dankbar und überwältigt, dass sich das alles so entwickelt hat. Gleichzeitig bedeutet das: All mein Herzblut steckt in diesem Projekt. Deshalb lege ich eine kleine Tattoo-Pause ein. Ab Dezember bin ich wieder voll da und freue mich auf euch alle.

INK AGAINST BORDERS geht 2025 in die dritte Runde. Laut, solidarisch, sichtbar.
Kleine Ideen können große Bewegungen werden wenn wir uns zusammentun.

ALERTA!

#inkagainstborders #flintatattoo #solidarity #seawatch

DQUnzczjbxp.content:
IAB 25 – It’s a wrap

Ich hab die letzten 48 Stunden nur geschlafen (und geheult) und denke immer noch, dass ich das alles nur geträumt habe. Ich bin sprachlos.
Samstagabend habe ich glaube ich zum ersten Mal realisiert, was da eigentlich passiert und wie groß das alles ist.
Ich wurde zwei Tage lang mit so viel Liebe überschüttet, dass ich nicht weiß, wohin damit.
Eine so große Veranstaltung. So viel Solidarität. So viele Artists. So viele verschiedene, individuelle, tolle Menschen. So viele Besucher:innen. Ausverkauft. Und trotzdem so ein safer Space mit unbeschreiblichen Vibes. Alle für einen gemeinsamen Zweck.

Unser Spendenziel wurde bei weitem übertroffen. Jeder Stress, jede Träne, jeder Nervenzusammenbruch der letzten Monate hat sich mehr als gelohnt und war es wert.

Ich habe keine Ahnung, wie ich das verarbeiten soll. Ich bin einfach nur dankbar für das, was wir da gemeinsam erleben durften. Dafür, zu sehen, was wir als FLINTA*s auf die Beine stellen können. Zu sehen wie viele wir sind.

Ich schlafe jetzt noch ein paar Tage weiter und versuche irgendwie wieder klarzukommen.

DANKE an jede einzelne beteiligte Person.
Ihr habt mein Herz und ich werde dieses Wochenende wahrscheinlich mein Leben lang nie vergessen.

Alerta!

#inkagainstborders

DH6cZvPyOgE.content:
Today is a special day for me. 17 years of tattooing! 
It marks 17 years since I finished my apprenticeship. It definitely hasn’t been an easy road, but my clients have made it worth it all. There’s been many ups and downs but I’m a fighter and these last few years have proved just that. 
I’ve learned so much about the industry and myself along the way, and will continue to learn more and more each day. 
I strive to become a better artist and person each day of my career and I value those who have stuck by my side from day one, or joined in along the way. I absolutely cherish you and wouldn’t be where I am without you. Thank you so much for all your trust, support and appreciation. The love is being sent right back at you! I truly value each and every one of you. 

Thank you to every tattoo shop that I’ve worked in and every tattoo artist that I’ve worked alongside with. Whether you have more experience or less experience than me, you’ve shaped me along the way. It could be positive or negative. Take it how you will. 
I will say this- We are a community and it’s important to have each other‘s backs, especially when times get tough. 💖

17 happens to be my ✨lucky✨ number, so this is an extra special one for me. 
Here’s to many more!

Now with that being said, come celebrate with me and book a tattoo with me. I love ya! Thank you for 17 amazing years! 🥺💖
XO -Sinner

C04GxkELuHs.content: 6 months sober today! 🌟🌟🌟 I don’t post much personal stuff on social media, but here it goes.  I had my last drink in June on the way back from a wedding. At a place I drank at often, in a town where I drank too much. I had been talking about quitting drinking for years, and after my 40th birthday, I finally did it. It took a couple of years to gradually quit by taking longer and longer breaks and only drinking alcohol that I liked. I used alcohol to deal with almost everything from sadness to happy events. It was a little bit of an emotional struggle finding out what to fill that void with. Who knew that I could just exercise and go outside 🙃. I didn’t realize how much I was using it to cope with daily life until I quit. Realizing what’s working and not working in my life right now is also a struggle. I’ve got a lot to work on, but at least I’m headed in the right direction. 6 months doesn’t seem like much in the scope of a lifespan, but it’s a start, and it’s something I thought I could never do. I’m not looking for any congratulations, I just wanted to share a life update ❤️ if anyone needs to talk or have someone checking in on them from time to time, Reach Out! I also have a ton of quit lit I can send or recommend to you. Thanks to the friends I’ve gotten support from it means everything. See you in June when I hit my 1 year 🥰 #soberliving #soberlife

C_2MCWdsOrx.content:
Hey there, how are you? I hope you have a coffee in hand and start to feel human again!

Im having tea and snuggling in my blanket while looking at yesterday's work: One of my regulars and favourite clients through my years in Bergen came by for his appointment yesterday and got some work done. 

He has had a challenging few years, and it was so good to see him again! I admire people a lot for how they can still smile and get through the day when life gets hard.

This work is an example of something I do a lot, but I dont really talk about it, and thats free hand drawing and tattooing. 

It is such a normal part of my day. I didn't really think about it as something to mention,  but then my darling Carmensita @@blekknroll reminded me that freehand is cool to share! And of course it is. To someone who does not tattoo every day, say a client, it might seem wild to just draw on someone with a marker and then tattoo that design without any other stencil or tool. 

But we do it a lot. For one: it's a tattoo so personal, so deeply in the ownership of the client that no other tattoo in the world is the same. The client gets to see it take shape then and there: and there is no doubt this came directly to them from the artist #no AI haha! But that is very special. 

And for the artist: to make a tattoo sice and shape flow with the body, one of the most helpful things is drawing on the actual body. 

You can draw something stunning on a piece of paper and then when you stick it on the client with a stencil sometimes it's looks wonky and weird: it looked fine on a flat surface ,but bot on the anatomy of the client!

So drawing on the body from the start helps get that flow and helps the artist make the tattoo work for the body shape very quickly!

I hope this was interesting, my friend:  I'm here to answer any questions you might have about this way of creating tattoos!

Thanks so much for checking in on me: you know it helps me and inspires me tons when you like my posts or share them with your people😀 it helps a lot in continuing my creative work!

Thanks so much, and have a great day!
XOXO-💕MissAnnlaug 💕

🥰Hei dere!😀Her er et prosjekt jeg har jobbet på i det siste. Det er ikke helt ferdig, men må måtte jeg bare vise det likevel!

Viss du blar gjennom bildene vil du se tegningen som ble gjort på planleggings timen sammen med bildet av det arbeidet vi har gjort til nå. 

Det kan være spennende å se hvordan det ser ut som tegning ved siden av resultatet. 💕🩷

Ofte på tegne timer blir det mye kaos på huden og feite streker som ser ut som en tusj spagetti. 
Men ut av det kommer en tatovering tilpasset kroppen på en unik måte og det er veldig viktig: formene er tilpasset personens anatomi. Det er derfor vi tegner rett på huden i planlegging fasen.

💌 Del med noen som du vet går med tattoo drømmer: det å komme å ha en konsultasjon er gratis! Full tegnetime koster litt, men er en god måte å komme i havn på hva man vil ha. 

Små og mellomstore tatoveringer er jeg også utrolig glad i. Store prosjekter er kjekt, men de små eller mellomstore gir helt andre kreative utfordringer og jeg ELSKER å lage de! Ikke tenk at din tattoo ide er for " liten og kjedelig". Det er den ikke.💜

It was an absolute🧡 pleasure 🧡to finish off this project this week. My client wanted to tell the story of the goddesses of the norse mythology without being too obvious. 

After a lot of prep work, we came up with this design, and I am thrilled to share it with you all!

Telling stories and expressing something that lives only in the imagination through a drawing, a painting, or a tattoo is absolutely magical. 

Bringing into view what can't be seen: the stuff of dreams, nightmares, and fairytales: that's what this is all about!

Art is very personal. But I have decided to start sharing my art as much as I can, when ever I can. The time has come to fully accept the fact that I am an artist, not just a tattoo artist.🩷

I have neglected my need and desire to paint too much and for too long.💔 Making excuses because I was tired, swamped with tattoo related tasks or what ever. It doesn't matter anymore. 💫

The truth is, I was born to paint. And doing it again has cracked me open in ways I could not have predicted. 

💫Healing old wounds,
💫 being overwhelmed with the desire to create and develop, 
💫feeling a lot of calm and joy in the work: 

💜its all been there the whole time waiting for me.💜

I guess I just had to grow up properly before I let myself be a child again. 

"Mollo" was my childhood nickname that my mom gave me. Im taking it back full force now and giving that little girl permission to do what she dreamed to do!

Thank you all for your contributions support of my creative work. Without you I would have never reached this point. I mean that.

Last night, we celebrated a woman who embodies courage, conviction, and compassion, Desiree Perez, CEO and Co-Founder of @rocnation, we presented her with The Gathering for Justice’s Harry Belafonte Social Justice Award at our 20th Anniversary Gala.

In my speech, I shared that "When Harry Belafonte created The Gathering for Justice, he did so because he believed that artists, leaders, and visionaries carried not just influence, but responsibility, the responsibility to speak truth, to move culture toward justice, and to lift the voices too often left unheard.

Our next honoree embodies that spirit in every way. Through her leadership at Roc Nation, Team Roc, and the United Justice Coalition, Desiree Perez has redefined what it means to lead with both power and principle.

Desiree is a woman who doesn’t just sit at the table, she builds it, and she makes sure others have a seat too. Through UJC, she has united artists, athletes, lawyers, and advocates to take on some of the most urgent issues of our time , from criminal justice reform to economic equity, reminding us that when culture and activism meet, transformation follows."

When I first met Desiree nearly a decade ago, I saw myself in her, a Latina navigating spaces not built for us, yet determined to create our own tables. Her strength reminded me of what it means to lead with purpose and principle, even when the path is lonely.

In a world already so divided, it is vital that we uplift one another, especially as women, as Latinas, as leaders carrying generations of stories and struggle. Our liberation is interdependent, our success intertwined.

To my sister in this work, Desiree, thank you for your light, your partnership, and your leadership. You honor Mr. B’s legacy by living the truth he stood for: “When you stand for justice, you stand for humanity.”

DQxdspjiRgO.content:
There’s a particular kind of fear that settles in your bones when you realize your body, your brown skin, your accent, your existence, has been marked as suspicious. When the simple act of living, of loving your family, of driving to work, can make you a target.

Lately, I find myself, and my own family, walking around with our passports in hand, as if a piece of paper could prove our belonging. We carry them like armor, hoping they might protect us if questioned, detained, or profiled.

But deep down we know, it won’t save us.
Because to them, our brown skin still reads as foreign. Our existence still feels like a threat.

A U.S. citizen detained while his toddler cries in the backseat.
A pastor shot by ICE while pleading for mercy.
Children zip-tied on the pavement.
A father having a seizure while clinging to his baby.
A mother dying in detention, her newborn laid on her chest.
A daycare teacher dragged away in front of terrified children.
ICE agents firing on a man warning them that kids were arriving for school.

They call it law and order.
We feel it as fear and humiliation.

We deserve to live without that weight, without having to prove our right to be here, to breathe, to exist.

Because we didn’t cross the border, the border crossed us. And our ancestors crossed back to reclaim what was already, rightfully, ours.

For every family that clutches papers like lifelines, for every child taught to “stay calm if they stop us,” for every ancestor who crossed borders so we could live free, we remember:

Our existence is not the crime.
The system is!

DRLjAdBDXI_.content:
It’s taken me some time to process the news of @aquilbasheer3  passing. Part of me felt that if I didn’t open Facebook or IG, if I didn’t see the posts, maybe it wouldn’t be real. But grief doesn’t work that way, it sits with you until you find the courage to face it.

I met Aquil through my mentor Nane, when I was doing violence-prevention work through Barrios Unidos and from the very beginning he treated me like family. Years later while I was leading The Gathering, we traveled together on a delegation to support the peace process in El Salvador. My Spanish wasn’t perfect back then, but somehow I became his interpreter, 🤦🏻‍♀️ and he trusted me anyway. That was Aquil. He had a way of seeing your spirit before your résumé and your heart before your titles.

He often made space for me in rooms where too few women, and too few young leaders were taken seriously. And he always showed up when I called on him, whether it was a nonviolence training. a panel in Oxnard, a concert at the Greek Theater or just to come see him in LA. 

Losing him is heavy not just for me but for our whole community. Aquil was a powerful force, a teacher, a protector, a visionary, and a man who dedicated his life to interrupting cycles of violence and building bridges where others only saw walls.

I’m grateful for the time we shared, for the lessons, and for the love. May his memory be a blessing and may we carry forward the legacy he lived every single day.

Rest in power, Aquil! ✊🏽✊🏽✊🏽

DR-IyObiMfU.content:
There’s a dangerous lie in this country that immigrants “get everything.”

Let me set the record straight.

Immigrants don’t arrive in the United States and immediately receive comfort, security, or opportunity. What many receive instead is suspicion, exploitation, and silence.

People call us uneducated, dirty, say we don’t belong. That couldn’t be further from the truth.

Many immigrants arrive with degrees: engineers, teachers, nurses, accountants, credentials earned through sacrifice and discipline. But those degrees are often not recognized here. So people swallow their pride and work in factories, in the fields, in restaurants, in warehouses, cleaning homes, caring for elders, raising other people’s children. Not because they lack intelligence or ambition, but because survival doesn’t wait for validation.

Immigrants work some of the hardest jobs in this country, for the lowest wages, with the least protection. Many pay taxes they will never benefit from. Many live with constant fear, of a broken tail light, a knock at the door, a system that would rather discard them than protect them.

And yes, many are returning home. Because they were kicked out of this country after it was stolen from the US. 

Let’s be honest: this country runs on immigrant labor while denying immigrant humanity.

Belonging isn’t something you get to gatekeep. Education doesn’t disappear at borders. Worth doesn’t depend on papers. And hard work has never been the problem.

The problem is a system willing to benefit from immigrants while refusing to see them as fully human.

We are not the lie you’ve been told.
We are the backbone you depend on.
And we belong, whether you’re comfortable with that or not. Stop telling yourselves lies to mask your racism and prejudice towards us! ✊🏽 RP @brownissues

DT46Z_ljnFX.content:
I keep thinking about Liam.

He’s five.
In kindergarten.
Still has all his baby teeth.
Still believes grown-ups will do the right thing.

I have a five-year-old too. His name is Damacio.

They’re the same age.
Same grade.
Same smile.
Same brown skin.
Same hope tucked into their small bodies.

When I drop Damacio off at school, I watch him walk in with his backpack bouncing, already thinking about recess and snacks and whatever small adventure the day will bring. I expect to pick him up. I assume he’ll come home.

Liam didn’t.

Instead, he stood outside his home in the cold while adults with power refused every option that would have kept him safe. His mother was inside. Neighbors were there. School officials begged to take him. Someone kept saying, “I will take the child.”

And still, ICE took him.

People are arguing about policy and procedure. But Liam is not a policy.

He’s a little boy who should have been allowed to go inside his home, take off his shoes, and ask what's for dinner.

When I look at his face, I see my son. I see how easily this could be Damacio. How easily it could be any of our children.

This is what breaks me:
Five-year-old black and brown boys don’t get the benefit of innocence.
They get suspicion.
They get handled.

No child deserves this type of treatment.

Liam deserves to be home.
He deserves to feel safe.
He deserves a childhood that doesn’t include fear.

And so does my son.
And so do yours.

Two years ago today, Hind Rajab’s dreams were stolen.

She dreamed of becoming a doctor, to help people, to heal. She loved the sea. She loved the color pink. She loved her family. She loved to play. She was a child, exactly as children everywhere are: full of tenderness, curiosity, and big dreams for a future she never got to live.

This portrait is a moment of remembrance, and an act of refusal. Refusal to let her be reduced to a statistic. Refusal to let the world look away.

Hind’s story, told in The Voice of Hind Rajab (@thevoiceofhindrajabfilm), is not an exception. It is the story of tens of thousands of Palestinian children whose names we will never know, whose dreams were never recorded, whose lives were stolen in silence.

Remembering Hind is a call to action, to do everything in our power to protect and fight for the millions of Palestinian children who are still trying to live. To show up and demand every child be afforded the right to live. To play. To hope. To dream. To live in dignity and not constant fear.

Today and every day, we remember Hind and every child who has been killed and every child who needs us to show up for them.

In honor of Hind and all children, we will be selling a limited run of signed prints with proceeds going to the Palestine Red Crescent Society. Link to purchase can be found in bio. RP @obeygiant

DV58ikUEcPw.content:
Almost 15 years ago, Mr. Belafonte sent me to Mexico to find my roots.

When I arrived in Zacatecas to meet my parents for their wedding anniversary, my father had our driver stop in the middle of the highway so he could show me an agave plant growing in the fields. The man tending the agave cut a piece and my father handed it to me to taste.

Standing there, he told me the beautiful story of the agave, how for centuries it has sustained Mexico. How our people used it for food, medicine, fiber, and for the spirits that bring families and communities together. A plant that survives in the harshest conditions, rooted deep in the earth, resilient and enduring.

That moment stayed with me. It was about more than a plant. It was about understanding where we come from, the land that nourished our ancestors, and the quiet strength that runs through our story as Mexicans.

When I returned to Mexico City last year and saw agave again growing beside bold modern architecture, I was reminded of that day on the highway with my father. How the past and present live side by side in Mexico. How our roots remain, even as we continue to grow. Circa March 2025 📷 by @argelia23

DVit3UugHqM.content: Those of you who know me know I'm for kindness to ourselves and Earth first. I'm sorta wild in the forest sense. Don't wear plastic, and hate the plastic bags mushrooms are grown in. I haven't solved everything, but our oysters are grown in reusable buckets. But lions mane has been trickier to ditch the bags. I thought. I have tried buckets and runs but since the accident can't lift heavy sawdust out of a sterilizer. So I tried jars. Super easy. Honestly it's easier than bags. I didn't even fully sterilize these jars of locally milled sawdust. I didn't do it long enough. The mycelium didn't care. Colonized quick. As always, it's just grain spawn on millet put into a sterilized sorta jar of sawdust and incubated a week. I put them in the room with the lids cracked for a week before removing the lid. I left a hole in the middle of the sawdust in the PC and put a spoonful of spawn in it. Voila.

DW2WzG1lDhI.content:
More swarm traps!
Why catch wild #bees? 
Well, hopefully they come from bees in trees, not bees from neighbors. That means the colony they came from lived without being fed or treated for at least a season. So we are collecting varroa and disease resistant genetics to keep from feeding sugar (the bees have good foraging timing and instinct for raising babies at appropriate times) and treating with mitucides (the bees can handle a parasite load and can clean themselves). 
Even organic bees can be fed sugar and are almost always treated for mites. They say it's essential oils or plant derived, but what they don't tell you is it's synthetic oils and super strong. Also expensive. And then the sugar feeding. Which is wild. I may be on a learning curve not treating my bees that way, but it will pay off. My goat herd is treatment free too. So are my birds and bunnies. It took a few years to learn how to keep them healthy. So in a few years I'll get it with the bees too. 
My birds sleep in trees. My bunnies sleep in holes in the ground. Our goats eat wild foods. I'm sure it's possible with the bees to get out of the treatment system. It's genetics and husbandry.

DVwQWXOgnEh.content:
Der „Kontextmismatch“ (Kontext-Missverhältnis) in der Psychologie beschreibt bei Diaspora-Gemeinschaften während eines Krieges in der Heimat das Phänomen, dass die psychische Realität der Migranten im neuen Land drastisch von der täglichen Lebenswirklichkeit der Menschen im Kriegsgebiet abweicht. Dies führt zu spezifischen psychischen Belastungen, Identitätskrisen und oft zu einer „unsichtbaren“ Traumatisierung, da die Betroffenen physisch in Sicherheit sind, psychisch aber im Krieg leben.

Auswirkungen auf die Psyche:

Trauma trotz Distanz: Diaspora-Mitglieder erleben „indirekte Traumatisierung“ durch den ständigen Kontakt mit Nachrichten, Videos und Schilderungen aus dem Kriegsgebiet.

Chronische Angst und Depression: Die ständige Sorge um Angehörige, die Ungewissheit und die mediale Konfrontation mit Gewalt führen zu Schlafstörungen, Angststörungen und Depressionen.

Entfremdung: Die Diskrepanz zwischen der „normalen“ Welt des Aufnahmelandes und der apokalyptischen Realität der Heimat erzeugt ein Gefühl der Entfremdung von der neuen Umgebung.

Quellen:

https://www.unwomen.org/en/articles/explainer/inside-the-crisis-you-dont-see-how-war-impacts-womens-mental-health#:~:text=Almost%20everyone%20affected%20by%20a,)%2C%20bipolar%20disorder%20or%20schizophrenia.

https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391506314_The_Psychological_Impact_of_War_on_Immigrants_Public_Health_Strategies_for_Support

DWwvyA8ARMP.content:
“Kaeru” block prints hopping to @nc_cbf SF Cherry Blossom Festival next weekend! 

Frogs were a significant part of my life while I was growing up in San Jose, a creek (all walled in cement but still one of the area’s natural paths for a creek) runs behind my family’s home and every spring, we would start to hear ribbits from the creek until it would grow into a chorus and we would see tiny green frogs hopping around our backyard. My sibling, family, friends, and I would spend many evenings catching frogs in the backyard and playing ping pong. They would love to hop into the house even and we’d have to let them back outside. These frogs helped teach me how to care for the natural world we’re all a part of. “Kaeru” means frog in Japanese and it also means “to return home,” which struck me as so fitting for these little creatures. Even though now the county doesn’t leave the creek “on” enough to allow the frogs to return, I still think of them often and they remind me of home.
